items.problem: Skill prescribes `winapp build`, a non-existent CLI command, wasting a turn every migration.
items.evidence: session-log turn 63: `winapp build` → "'build' was not matched"; recovered with `dotnet build` turn 64. lessons.json doc_errors[0].
items.root_cause: Plugin moved to native dotnet build/run but instruction sites still name the removed `winapp build` wrapper.
items.change: Replaced all `winapp build` references with `dotnet build` (sync + exit sentinel) in SKILL.md (Steps 3, 4, build-discipline note), Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 header, and MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md WUI section; added an explicit 'there is no winapp build subcommand' note.
items.expected_effect: Agent compiles with a real command on the first try; no wasted 'build not matched' turn.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, no `'build' was not matched` line appears in the build log and the final compile uses `dotnet build`.

items.problem: Copied UWP Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs triggers CS0579 duplicate-attribute build failures.
items.evidence: session-log turns 56-59: 6x CS0579 at obj\...\AssemblyInfo.cs; fixed by removing the copied file. lessons.json errors_encountered[0].
items.root_cause: SDK-style WinUI 3 projects auto-generate assembly attributes (GenerateAssemblyInfo=true) that collide with a hand-written AssemblyInfo.cs carried over from UWP.
items.change: Added a 'CS0579 Duplicate Attribute (copied Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs)' section to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md with a delete-the-file Get-ChildItem snippet and a do-not-set-GenerateAssemblyInfo-false caveat.
items.expected_effect: Agent recognizes CS0579 immediately and deletes the copied file instead of diagnosing from scratch.
items.falsifiable_check: On a scenario whose UWP source has Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs, no CS0579 errors survive to a failed build (file removed during migration).

items.problem: In-process windows.backgroundTasks/windows.appService <Extension> manifest entries fail AppX deployment (0x80080204).
items.evidence: session-log turn 60: 'EntryPoint="Tasks.SampleBackgroundTask" without ActivatableClassId ... (0x80080204)'; fixed turn 61. lessons.json errors_encountered[1].
items.root_cause: Packaged WinUI 3 desktop apps don't auto-generate the windows.activatableClass.inProcessServer/ActivatableClass registration UWP's toolchain produced, so an in-process EntryPoint resolves to nothing and the manifest is rejected.
items.change: Added item 5 to the manifest checklist in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md: drop in-process background-task/app-service <Extension> blocks for structural migrations (C# class still compiles), or author the full activatable-class registration and otherwise defer.
items.expected_effect: Agent removes/handles the offending <Extension> proactively; smoke launch passes without a manifest-validation detour.
items.falsifiable_check: On a background-task/app-service scenario, the first winapp run does not emit a 0x80080204 manifest validation error.

deferred_to_human: Validate-UwpMigration smoke launch reports a genuine manifest defect (0x80080204) as a non-fatal WARN labelled 'environment/deploy issue'. Consider distinguishing manifest-validation failures from true environment failures so they FAIL the gate — left for human review as it borders on changing the measurement policy.
